`sprigctl` is the operator's command-line tool: clusters, tenants, settings, indexes, approvals, moves, failover and the rest of the Admin API.

## `sprigctl`

```text
SprigDB operator CLI

Usage: sprigctl [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  dc               Data centers
  cluster          MariaDB clusters
  tenant           Tenants
  settings         See and change settings at every scope [alias: config]
  index            Automatic indexes and recommendations
  recommendations  Recommendations held for approval, and their policies
  explain          Explain a query fingerprint, a decision or a tenant's placement
  shard            Shards
  job              Mover jobs
  advisor          The sharding advisor
  gateway          Gateways of the DC
  check            Operational checks
  logic            Logic functions
  space            Spaces and shares
  inherit          Inherited tables, shares, tree-wide ids and the references that refuse deletes
  txn              In-doubt distributed transactions
  sink             Sinks: list, show, pause, resume, reset, dead letters, connections
  graph            Graphs
  search           Search indexes and their copies on workers
  login            Log in as a named operator; the session is kept per endpoint
  logout           End this endpoint's login session
  whoami           Who the Admin API takes you for
  operator         Named platform and DC operators
  token            Tokens you issue for scripts and services
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --client-cert <client-cert>  For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --client-key <client-key>    The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --dc <dc>                    Data center to act in
  -o, --output <output>            Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --dry-run                    Show what would change
      --yes                        Don't ask for confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version
```

### `sprigctl cluster`

```text
MariaDB clusters

Usage: sprigctl cluster [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  register      Check an existing MariaDB cluster and register it with SprigDB
  list          List the DC's clusters
  show          Show a cluster: nodes, health, capability profile, gaps
  probe         Probe a cluster now and publish what changed
  drain         Stop placing on a cluster and move its shards away
  retire        Retire a drained cluster's record; probes stop
  set-nodes     Change a cluster's node addresses: nodes named get the new address, new ids are added
  extract       Extract a diverged former writer's transactions (row images, sealed) to the workers' extract store
  rebuild       Rebuild a node from a replica's backup and attach it to the writer
  extract-open  Print a sealed errant extract as JSON lines (needs the workers' key file)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --client-cert <client-cert>  For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --client-key <client-key>    The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --dc <dc>                    Data center to act in
  -o, --output <output>            Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --dry-run                    Show what would change
      --yes                        Don't ask for confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

#### `sprigctl cluster register`

```text
Check an existing MariaDB cluster and register it with SprigDB

Usage: sprigctl cluster register [OPTIONS] [name]

Arguments:
  [name]  A name unique in the DC

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
  -f, --file <file>                A TOML file with dc, name, topology, endpoints or nodes, credentials_ref, capacity, declared
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --topology <topology>        The cluster's topology [possible values: galera, primary_replica, replication, single, single_node, external]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --node <node>                A node as [id=]host:port; repeat for each, the writer first
      --client-cert <client-cert>  For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --credentials <credentials>  Credentials reference with [sprig_ctl] and [sprig_repl] tables: file:<path> or env:<name>
      --client-key <client-key>    The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --ctl-secret <ctl-secret>    sprig_ctl's credential reference
      --dc <dc>                    Data center to act in
      --repl-secret <repl-secret>  sprig_repl's credential reference
      --declare <declare>          A TOML file of [declared] facts
  -o, --output <output>            Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --dry-run                    Show what would change
      --memory-gb <memory-gb>      Server memory, GB (recorded; not used yet)
      --storage-gb <storage-gb>    Storage, GB (for placement)
      --yes                        Don't ask for confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

### `sprigctl tenant`

```text
Tenants

Usage: sprigctl tenant [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  create     Create a tenant and bootstrap its catalog (returns once active)
  list       List tenants
  show       Show a tenant: state, ancestry, catalog cluster and versions
  delete     Delete a leaf tenant and drop its catalog
  user       A tenant's users, created by an operator (inside the tenant, CREATE USER does the same)
  export     Export a tenant: schemas, rows, users and grants, settings
  import     Load a tenant export into a tenant and verify checksums and grants
  settings   The tenant's own setting rows (tenant, database and object scope)
  pin        Pin a tenant to its cluster and DC: the balancer won't move it; drains and residency changes report it as blocked
  unpin      Let the balancer manage a pinned tenant again
  suspend    Suspend a tenant and its subtree: logins fail with 39303, open sessions close (auth.close_sessions_on_revoke), triggers, sinks and schedules wait
  resume     Resume a suspended tenant: logins and background work start again
  move       Move a tenant to another data center, online
  traffic    A tenant's traffic by client data center, and the move it suggests
  failover   Fail a tenant over to its standby in another data center
  standby    Record a standby of a tenant: a cluster in another data center that replicates its home cluster
  residency  Show or set a tenant's data residency
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
```

```text
  set       Set a value at one scope
  reset     Remove a value (or bounds) at one scope; narrower scopes then inherit [alias: unset]
  bounds    Limit what narrower scopes may set; parts not named are kept
```

### `sprigctl index`

```text
Automatic indexes and recommendations

Usage: sprigctl index [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list             List automatic indexes (live ones; --all adds dropped and rejected)
  show             One index: definition, evidence, validations, history
  recommendations  Recommendations waiting for approval (recommend mode, advice)
  approve          Roll a recommendation out as an automatic index [alias: apply]
  reject           Turn a recommendation down (not recommended again for a while) [alias: dismiss]
  drop             Drop an automatic index from every shard
  pin              Freeze an automatic index in its state [alias: freeze]
  unpin            Let automatic indexing manage a pinned index again
  restore          Make a retiring (IGNORED) index visible again, or recreate a user index dropped for disuse, and pin it
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --client-cert <client-cert>  For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --client-key <client-key>    The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --dc <dc>                    Data center to act in
  -o, --output <output>            Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --dry-run                    Show what would change
      --yes                        Don't ask for confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

#### `sprigctl index list`

```text
List automatic indexes (live ones; --all adds dropped and rejected)

Usage: sprigctl index list [OPTIONS] --tenant <tenant>

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>        Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --tenant <tenant>            The tenant [env: SPRIGCTL_TENANT=]
      --db <db>                    Only this database
      --token-file <token-file>    A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --table <table>              Only this table
      --client-cert <client-cert>  For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --state <state>              Only this state: validating, recommended, rolling_out, observing, active, retiring, dropping, dropped, rejected, failed, frozen
      --client-key <client-key>    The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --recommended                Only recommendations (as `index recommendations`)
      --all                        Also dropped and rejected indexes (history)
      --dc <dc>                    Data center to act in
  -o, --output <output>            Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --dry-run                    Show what would change
      --yes                        Don't ask for confirmation
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

#### `sprigctl check no-restart`

```text
Change settings, listeners and certificates under load; prove no restart and no failed statement

Usage: sprigctl check no-restart [OPTIONS] --telemetry <telemetry> --gateway <gateway> --user <user> --password <password>

Options:
      --endpoint <endpoint>
          Admin API endpoint [default: http://127.0.0.1:7480] [env: SPRIGCTL_ENDPOINT=]
      --telemetry <telemetry>
          The gateway's telemetry base URL, http://host:9180
      --gateway <gateway>
          The gateway's MySQL or MariaDB listener for the load, host:port
      --token-file <token-file>
          A file holding the Admin API bearer token [env: SPRIGCTL_TOKEN_FILE=]
      --ca-file <ca-file>
          For an https:// endpoint: the CA (PEM) its certificate is checked against [env: SPRIGCTL_CA_FILE=]
      --user <user>
          Login, <tenant>.<user>
      --client-cert <client-cert>
          For an https:// endpoint that requires one: a client certificate (PEM) [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_CERT=]
      --password <password>
          Its password [env: SPRIGCTL_GATEWAY_PASSWORD]
      --client-key <client-key>
          The private key (PEM) of --client-cert [env: SPRIGCTL_CLIENT_KEY=]
      --tls-insecure
          Load over TLS accepting any certificate
      --connections <connections>
          Load connections [default: 4]
      --dc <dc>
          Data center to act in
  -o, --output <output>
          Output format [default: table] [possible values: table, json, yaml]
      --set <set>
          A setting change, key=value@scope (scope as --scope takes it)
      --dry-run
          Show what would change
      --listener <listener>
          A listener rebind, name=host:port
      --listener-scope <listener-scope>
          Where listener.<name>.bind is written [default: dc]
      --yes
          Don't ask for confirmation
      --rotate-cert <rotate-cert>
          live.pem=new.pem: replace the gateway's certificate file
      --rotate-key <rotate-key>
          live-key.pem=new-key.pem: its key, replaced first
      --settle <settle>
          Seconds to wait after each change [default: 5]
  -h, --help
          Print help
```
